Open the map page

1
East-West pipeline hit, Medina region (9 Nov)
Saudi Energy Ministry: an attack caused a limited fire on the pipeline in the Medina region, put out with operations unaffected; exact spot not given (approximate).
2
Missiles intercepted over Riyadh (10 Nov)
The coalition says a ballistic and a cruise missile were downed over Riyadh on 10 Nov, after debris damaged the Aramco Tower on 8 Nov; no output loss reported.
3
10 Hormuz crossings (10 Nov), 5 dark
Windward counted 10 crossings on 10 Nov (one tanker) against 84-140 a day pre-war; Kpler put October Hormuz crude at about 10.2 mb/d, 60% of pre-war (area approximate).
4
UAE exports ~4.4 mb/d (9 Nov), up from 3.2
A UAE official says exports are almost 4.4 mb/d vs 3.1-3.2 mb/d before the war, helped by the Habshan-Fujairah pipeline that avoids Hormuz.
5
Tanker struck 19 nm NE of Lima (10 Nov)
UKMTO: a tanker was struck about 19 nm north-east of Lima, Oman, crew safe; the same afternoon ADNOC said one of its vessels was damaged in UAE waters and the IRGC claimed three tankers hit (unconfirmed).
6
57 ships holding in Gulf (10 Nov), down from 197
straits.live counted 57 AIS-visible ships holding in the Strait and Gulf watch box at 18:00 UTC on 10 Nov, against 54 on 9 Nov and 197 on 4 Nov; AIS coverage varies (area approximate).
7
Bypass routes >40% of Gulf exports
Kpler: pipelines avoiding Hormuz carry over 40% of regional exports vs 17% pre-war; Yanbu loadings 2.21 mb/d in 1-25 Oct vs 2.54 in September.
GULF OIL FLOWS · updated 11 Nov 2026

Less oil is leaving the Gulf than before the war: Kpler counts about 16.1 mb/d of crude across Hormuz, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Oman in October, of which only about 10.2 mb/d went through Hormuz itself, about 60% of the 17.1 mb/d pre-war level. Traffic through the strait stays very thin (Windward: 10 crossings on 10 Nov, half of them dark, with just one tanker), so bypass routes carry over 40% of exports and the UAE says its exports have risen to almost 4.4 mb/d via Fujairah. Attacks went on despite talk of a deal: on 10 Nov UKMTO reported a tanker struck about 19 nm north-east of Lima, Oman, ADNOC said one of its vessels was damaged in UAE waters, and the IRGC claimed three more tankers hit, a day after the East-West pipeline was hit in the Medina region. Trump calls the war 'effectively over' and says new strikes are unlikely, but Iran denies any talks, and Brent sits near two-month lows around $92.
